title: Ashfall Keep: an AI-assisted tower-defence game, and the UI problems screenshots didn’t reveal
author: Key_Art_9961
selftext:
Disclosure: I’m sharing this as Knowhubs, the creator of Ashfall Keep. This is a commercial game post. It uses AI-assisted coding and original AI-generated bitmap art.

The game combines six tower types with a Warden you can move around the battlefield. The AI workflow has involved generating and revising code and artwork, then testing the resulting build in a browser and feeding specific problems back into development. The most useful feedback has often been about what happens between the screenshots.

One phone report was especially concrete: tapping an empty foundation also placed a tower and spent gold. A build menu could look correct in a still image while the interaction was wrong. That turned into a precise check: the first tap should open choices and leave the gold balance unchanged; placing a tower needs a separate choice. The current revision addresses that interaction, though physical-phone verification is still ongoing.

Animation and visual communication raised similar questions. Feedback called out towers that did not visibly turn towards targets, enemies that appeared to float, and the Warden’s health bar covering her face. Having a detailed generated sprite did not answer whether players could read the action. These reports have been useful for keeping the revision work tied to visible behaviour rather than simply generating more assets.

The current In Development release is on itch.io. The free browser demo is The Broken Gate: one stage, five waves and all six tower choices. The full desktop download is US$1.99, with five worlds and 25 authored stages. Desktop is recommended, and progress is stored locally; export a save before changing browser or updating.

Demo and full-game details: [https://knowhubs.itch.io/ashfall-keep](https://knowhubs.itch.io/ashfall-keep)

For others using AI in a game-development workflow, how are you testing touch interactions and animation readability once the initial build looks convincing? I’d also welcome concrete reports from the opening stage: device, browser, what you tapped and what happened.
